checks_run: Inventoried 64 candidate files, checked file types and symlinks, parsed all 32 Python files, and reviewed learner, evaluator, reference, provenance, and validation material.

Ran the documented learner test command with the environment default Python and reran public, sealed, and adversarial suites against the reference with the supplied Python 3.11.5 interpreter and a reviewer-owned TMPDIR.
Ran the starter sentinel, CLI help, namespace capability probe, and structural validator.
Ran independent edge probes for argv type determinism, finite timeout enforcement, launch-failure state recovery, and image-layer digest binding.
Compared the candidate aggregate file digest before and after review to verify immutability.
evidence: Reference execution passed 18/18 public, 22/22 sealed, and 4/4 adversarial authored tests; the intentional starter sentinel failed with NotImplementedError.

The manifest honestly remains GENERATED/PARTIAL, requires independent validation, and sets productionized=false; documentation explicitly disclaims fuzzing, benchmarking, full namespace execution, hostile-workload safety, and production readiness.
Runner accepts NaN and infinity timeout values, so its claimed execution bound can be disabled.

A syntactically valid custom backend tuple containing a NUL argument caused uncaught ValueError after the durable RUNNING transition, leaving history at CREATED to RUNNING rather than recording FAILED.
ContainerSpec accepted sets and generators despite R1 requiring tuple/list; set-backed argv order changed across PYTHONHASHSEED values.
A controlled mutation between layer application and hashing produced rootfs bytes from layer A while manifest layer_sha256 identified replacement layer B.
The documented python3 learner command selected Python 3.6.8 in this workspace and failed with five import errors; Python 3.11.5 was available only through the explicit supplied path.
Answers were found only below sealed/, no symlinks were present, manifest/provenance identifiers were internally consistent, and no unsafe tar extraction or shell=True call site was found.
limitations: No populated root filesystem was supplied, so the successful rootless-user-namespace probe does not validate mount, PID, UTS, IPC, chroot, or workload isolation.
No fuzz campaign, benchmark run, hostile concurrent rootfs mutation test, production review, or transfer verification was performed; no corresponding label is awarded.

The upstream linked repository and source history could not be compared because network access is restricted and git is unavailable, so the no-copy and linked-license assertions remain provenance claims rather than independently established facts.
The review workspace exposes evaluator and sealed files by design; enforcement of their exclusion from an actual learner view was not available to test.
Default system temporary directories were unavailable; tempfile-based checks were rerun successfully with a reviewer-owned writable TMPDIR.
